name: export_graph_svg
docs: Draw a fully laid-out, fully styled diagram to a standalone SVG string. Pure draw: the caller
supplies exact on-screen geometry and styling, so the export matches what's on screen.

args.title: StyledGraph
args.description: A fully laid-out, fully styled diagram, ready to draw with no further layout decisions.

edges_on_top.description:
Draw edges (and their markers/dots) AFTER nodes, so border-centered markers sit on top
of node borders (OC-Declare). Default: edges underneath, like React Flow's default.

StyledNode.description: One node in a [`StyledGraph`]: final position/size plus all of its own styling.

marking_dy.description:
Vertical offset of the marking row from the node center, in px (e.g. OC-Declare draws
its involvement dots below the label).

oneOf.description: Rounded rectangle. `radius` is the corner radius in px (0 = sharp corners).
Ellipse inscribed in the node's `w`x`h` box.
Circle of diameter `w` (h is ignored).

StyledLabel.description:
One line of text drawn centered in a node, offset vertically by `dy`. Multiple labels stack
(e.g. an activity name line + a frequency-count line below it).

dy.description: Vertical offset from the node center, in px.

dx.description: Horizontal offset from the node center, in px (e.g. to re-center a text+bullet group).

wrap.description:
Word-wrap to fit the node width (max 2 lines, ellipsized). Off by default: pass one
`StyledLabel` per pre-wrapped line instead when the caller already knows the split.

bullet.description:
Small kind-indicator glyph drawn just left of the text (OCEL type graph: square = event
type, dot = object type); ignored on wrapped labels.

bullet_color.description: Bullet fill; defaults to the label color.

oneOf.description: Filled circle (e.g. initial-marking token).
Faded square (e.g. final-marking token).

MarkingGroup.description:
A group of same-kind tokens drawn inside a node (e.g. Petri place markings), left-to-right in
a single row; if the total count doesn't fit the node's width, the row collapses to a numeral.

dashed.description: Draw a dashed border on each dot (OC-Declare optional involvement, min 0).

radius.description:
Fixed dot radius. When any group sets it, the whole row renders in exact mode: fixed
sizes, tight per-group clusters, no fit-to-node scaling or numeral collapse.

step.description:
Center-to-center spacing between this group's dots (exact mode; below `2*radius`
overlaps them into a cluster). Defaults to a non-overlapping `2*radius + 2`.

stroke.description:
Ring stroke around each dot (exact mode). Absent: ring only when `dashed`, in the
node's stroke color.

scale.description:
Icon half-size as a fraction of the node's half-extent. Defaults to the terminal-chrome
proportions used on screen (~0.3 of the radius).

IconKind.description:
A single decorative glyph drawn centered in a node (e.g. the start/end terminal chrome on a
DFG). Distinct from [`MarkingGroup`], which draws a *counted row* of tokens.

oneOf.description: "Play" triangle (start terminal).
"Stop" square (end terminal).

StyledEdge.description: One edge in a [`StyledGraph`]: an already-routed polyline plus its own styling.

points.description: Routed polyline points, already in the same coordinate space as node `cx`/`cy`.

gradient.description:
Linear gradient stroke from the first to the last polyline point, used by OC-Declare
multi-object-type arcs; two or more stops override `color` on the path.

marker_color.description:
Marker fill; defaults to the edge color (OC-Declare draws all markers in one neutral
gray so the object-type color stays on the path itself).

marker_size.description:

name: layout_graph
docs: Lay out an arbitrary directed graph. Returns node centres + edge polylines; rendering is left to
the caller. Thin binding wrapper over the shared `viz_layout` engine.

args.title: GraphSpec
args.description:
A generic directed-graph layout request: sized nodes plus directed edges by node index.
Cycles, self-loops and multi-edges are handled. This is the same engine Petri/DFG use.

weights.description:
Optional per-edge importance (same length as `edges`); heavier edges lay out straighter
and shorter. Empty => all equal.

flow_edges.description: Flow layout: tighter gaps + terminal centring (`true`) vs classic gaps (`false`, default).

flow_diagonal.description:
Diagonal (flow) routing vs orthogonal straight-channel routing (`false`, default). Only
meaningful with `flow_edges`.

edge_label_sizes.description:
Optional `[width, height]` of each edge's mid-point label (same length/order as `edges`);
the layout reserves that space so labels don't overlap other edges/nodes.

thickness.description:
Optional per-edge drawn stroke width (same length/order as `edges`); port spreading keeps
adjacent thick strokes from visually merging. Empty => all 2.0.

tree.description: Tidy-tree layout instead of layered; input must be a rooted tree/forest, edges come back unrouted.

compact.description: Compact the cross axis after placement (order-preserving); for dense hub-and-spoke graphs like the OCEL type graph. Default `false`.

GraphNode.description:
One node in a generic graph-layout request. Only its size and shape matter to the layout;
labels/colors are the caller's concern (this binding returns geometry, not an image).

ellipse.description: Draw as an ellipse (arcs meet the outline) vs a box. Defaults to box.

pin.description: Pin to the first or last layer: `"first"` (source rank) or `"last"` (sink rank).

category.description:
Optional grouping id (e.g. an object type). Same-category nodes are held in a consistent
order across layers as a crossing-neutral tiebreak. Absent means no grouping.

seed.description:
Optional seed centre `[x, y]` in final space. When any node has a seed, the layout keeps
the structural layer/order but places the cross-axis at the seed (a stable relayout).

pinned.description:
Hard-pin this node's seed cross-coordinate (others yield around it); use for the just-dragged
node so it lands exactly where dropped. Only meaningful with `seed`.

clear_after.description:
Minimum clearance (px) to keep free beyond this node's border on the positive order side
(screen right in TB, screen bottom in LR): room for caller-drawn self-loops + labels.

return_type.title: GraphLayout
return_type.description:
Result of [`layout_graph`]: one centre per input node, one orthogonal/flow polyline per edge,
in the same order as the input. All coordinates in a single SVG-style space.

name: reroute_graph
docs: On-drop relayout: re-route edges over the caller's final node positions (each node's `seed` is its
current centre) without recomputing a layout. Node centres come back unchanged; only routes change.

name: get_event_timestamps
docs: Aggregate event timestamps into a fixed number of bins, grouped by activity.
Events without a valid timestamp are skipped; events without a recognized
activity are counted under `"UNKNOWN"`.

args.description: Options for [`get_event_timestamps`].

num_bins.description: Number of time bins to aggregate events into.

activity_key.description: Event attribute key used to identify the activity name.

timestamp_key.description: Event attribute key used to extract the timestamp.

return_type.description: Aggregated event counts per timestamp bin, grouped by activity.

activities.description: All distinct activity names found in the log.

Width of each bin in milliseconds, which is also the spacing of the bin centers.

name: get_object_attribute_changes
docs: Extract the attribute change history for a specific object.
Returns one trace per attribute, each containing the timestamped values
in the order they appear in the log. Returns an error if the object ID
is not found.

return_type.title: ObjectAttributeChanges
return_type.description: Time-stamped attribute change history for a single OCEL object.

traces.description:
Attribute change traces keyed by attribute name.

Each entry contains the chronological list of value changes
for that attribute.

AttributeChange.description: A single attribute value change at a point in time.

value.description: Attribute value at this point in time.

name: locel_oc_perf_sojourn_per_event
docs: Per-event sojourn time.
For each event with at least one directly-follows predecessor, the sojourn time is
`event_time - latest_predecessor_time` in integer microseconds. Returns one row
`(event_id, sojourn_us)` per qualifying event.
`top_k`: if `Some(k)`, return only the `k` rows with the largest `sojourn_us`, ties broken by
ascending event id, sorted descending. `None` returns every qualifying event.

name: locel_oc_perf_sync_per_event
docs: Per-event synchronization time and the delaying object.
For each event with at least one directly-follows predecessor, the synchronization time is
`max_predecessor_time - min_predecessor_time` in integer microseconds (the span between its
earliest and latest directly-preceding event). The delaying object is the object linking the
latest predecessor (ties broken by ascending object id).
Returns one row `(event_id, sync_us, delaying_object_id)` per qualifying event.
`top_k`: if `Some(k)`, return only the `k` rows with the largest `sync_us`, ties broken by
ascending event id, sorted descending. `None` returns every qualifying event.

name: locel_conversion_rate
docs: Conversion rate from `source_type` to `target_type` via O2O, restricted to targets touched by `activity`.
Returns the fraction of `source_type` objects that have at least one outgoing O2O edge to a
`target_type` object related (via E2O) to some event of the given event type. Returns `0.0`
if no `source_type` objects exist.

name: locel_event_object_type_counts
docs: Count E2O relationships per `(event_type, object_type)` pair.
Each entry is `(event_type, object_type, count)`. A single `(event, object)` pair connected
by multiple qualifiers contributes once per qualifier. Pairs with zero relations are omitted.
Result row order is unspecified.

name: extraction_column_domain_items
docs: Every distinct value of `table.column` in a source held in the registry.
The registry counterpart of `extraction_column_domain`: same answer, for a source whose bytes
the host already holds rather than one reachable by connection string. Without it a dropped
file could be extracted from but never inspected, so the editor could not offer the example
values a dynamic type name needs, and on wasm, where every source is byte-held, not at all.
`sources` maps source id to registry item id. Every entry other than `source_id` is ignored.

name: extraction_compile
docs: Compile `blueprint` into SQL views presenting the OCEL 2.0 surface over `catalog`'s tables,
with no connection opened and no row read.
`shape` picks the emitted layout: [`EmissionShape::PerType`] (one view per declared event/
object type, the layout external OCEL 2.0 tooling reads) or [`EmissionShape::Consolidated`]
(a single wide `events`/`objects`/... layout with the type as a column value). A mapping the
emitter cannot reproduce exactly is skipped and recorded in the result rather than failing the
whole compile.

args.title: Blueprint
args.description:
A declarative mapping from relational rows to an OCEL.

Carries no connection details and no schema snapshot: both are supplied by the caller, which
keeps a blueprint portable, shareable and free of secrets.

version.description: Schema version. Checked against [`super::MODEL_VERSION`] during validation.

on_missing_endpoint.description: What to do about relations naming a missing entity.

on_duplicate_object.description: What to do about a repeated object id.

IdRendering.description: How entity ids are rendered, for events and objects alike.

oneOf.description: Use the id expression's value verbatim.

Prefix the id with its type name, so ids from different types cannot collide.

Under this setting every relation endpoint must declare its type, since otherwise the
prefixed id cannot be rebuilt. Validation enforces that.

id.description: Unique id, referenced by other nodes and by mappings.

label.description: Display label. No semantic role.

NodeOp.description: One operation in the row graph.

oneOf.description: Read a table from a source.

source_id.description: Source id, resolved to a connection at execution time.

Inner-join two nodes on the given column pairs.

on.description: Column pairs, as `(left column, right column)`.

oneOf.description:
Concatenate the rows of several nodes, aligning columns by name.

`UNION ALL`, not `UNION`: dropping duplicates would drop the entities they produce. Output
columns are the union of the inputs' column names, and an input lacking one contributes
`Null`. Both are model semantics a compiler must reproduce.

Predicate.description:
A boolean test over one row.

Comparisons are typed: numbers compare numerically, so `amount > 0` means what it says
rather than comparing text. Any comparison involving `NULL` is false, including `NULL = NULL`.

Compare two operands.

A fixed value.

Literal.description:
A literal in a comparison or membership test.

Untagged in JSON, so `true`, `5`, `5.0` and `"x"` deserialize to the matching variant.
Order matters for `Boolean`, `Integer`, `Float` and `Text`, whose JSON shapes overlap only
with each other (a bare JSON boolean, number or string): boolean before integer before float
before text.

`Timestamp` is exempt from that ordering: it is a single-field object (`{"timestamp": "..."}`)
rather than a bare string, so its position does not matter and no ordinary string that happens
to parse as RFC 3339 is silently reclassified. A plain string against a timestamp column works
without it, through `Predicate::prepare`'s literal coercion.

It is also what coalesces a fan-out: over a join of orders and their items, a `None`
id makes one event per item, an id naming the order one event per order, still related
to every item. The repeated rows count as
[`MappingStats::deduplicated`](super::report::MappingStats::deduplicated) while
`objects` below is emitted for each.

oneOf.description: An object.

When the attribute values below were observed. `None` records them as static
values stamped at the Unix epoch.

oneOf.description: An event-to-object relation.
An object-to-object relation.

The first part that produces a value.

body.description:
A bare `SELECT` body with no `CREATE` wrapper, so the same text serves a view, a CTE and

mapping.description: The mapping this is about, or `None` for a whole-log check.

path.description:
The JSON path of the authored entry this mapping came from (see `desugar_with_paths`), so
a diagnostic points at what the author wrote rather than a position in the flattened
list.

describes.description:
What this mapping produces, derived from its target: `event "appoint officer"`,
`event -> object relation`, and so on. Present whether or not a `label` was typed.

oneOf.description:
Two objects claim one id under different types. The extractor keeps the first and reports
the collision, and the views keep both.
Two events claim one id. See [`Self::AmbiguousObjectIdentity`].

extractor writes the mapping's first row for an id and ignores later repeats. SQL rows

name: extraction_validate
docs: Check `blueprint` against `catalog` for problems decidable from the schema alone, such as an
unknown source or table, a node graph cycle, or a type-rendering rule the blueprint's own
`id_rendering` setting cannot satisfy.
An empty result means `blueprint` is safe to pass to [`extraction_run`],
[`extraction_run_to_duckdb`] or [`extraction_compile`]. All three call this internally and
refuse to run an invalid blueprint, so calling it first is for surfacing errors to a user
while they edit, not a required step before the others.
The two report a refusal differently, because they fail differently: the running bindings
return an error string, while [`extraction_compile`] always returns a [`CompiledOcel`] and
puts one entry per validation error in its `errors` array, with no relations emitted. This is
also the only place a blueprint's `version` is checked: the bindings deserialize a
[`Blueprint`] with plain serde, not `Blueprint::from_json`, so a blueprint from a newer model
version is caught here and nowhere else.

Literal.description:
A literal in a comparison or membership test.

Untagged in JSON, so `true`, `5`, `5.0` and `"x"` deserialize to the matching variant.
Order matters for `Boolean`, `Integer`, `Float` and `Text`, whose JSON shapes overlap only
with each other (a bare JSON boolean, number or string): boolean before integer before float
before text.

`Timestamp` is exempt from that ordering: it is a single-field object (`{"timestamp": "..."}`)
rather than a bare string, so its position does not matter and no ordinary string that happens
to parse as RFC 3339 is silently reclassified. A plain string against a timestamp column works
without it, through `Predicate::prepare`'s literal coercion.

return_type.title: ExtractionReport
return_type.description:
What [`extract`](super::extract::extract) produced, beyond the OCEL itself.

Serializable but not deserializable: [`ExtractionError`] carries `&'static str` fields (a
borrow no deserializer can manufacture), so this only ever crosses a bindings boundary
outbound, as a `#[register_binding]` return value.

per_mapping.description:
One entry per mapping executed, in desugared blueprint order: the order the author wrote
the mappings in, with each ordered group expanded in place. Not execution order,
which is multi-pass and grouped by node. Each entry's [`MappingRef::path`] names the
authored entry.

errors.description:
Non-fatal problems collected while running: a policy configured to error
(`on_duplicate_object: Error`, `on_missing_endpoint: Error`), or an attribute type two
mappings disagreed on. Extraction continues past these. See [`ExtractionError`] for what
aborts it instead.

Capped at [`MAX_REPORTED_ERRORS`], with the remainder counted in
[`errors_suppressed`](Self::errors_suppressed).

errors_suppressed.description:
Non-fatal problems the run hit past [`MAX_REPORTED_ERRORS`], which
[`errors`](Self::errors) therefore does not name. Zero for every run under the cap.

rows_materialized.description:
Rows every `Join`/`Union` materialisation this run performed produced, summed across
materialisations rather than peaked: an upper bound on peak buffered rows. A cached
materialisation is counted once, when computed.

Zero when no mapping's node graph contains a `Join` or `Union`, since a pure
`Source -> Filter` chain streams. Zero is therefore a witness that the run streamed.

pushdown_declined.description:
Nodes whose source could have executed the whole node but the compiler declined to build
the query for, paired with the reason, and deduplicated per node.

Always safe, since the executor runs the node itself. Reported because falling back on a
`Join` is the one execution path whose memory grows with the data, so this explains a
non-zero [`rows_materialized`](Self::rows_materialized).

finalize.description:
What the sink did at [`ExtractionSink::finalize`](super::sink::ExtractionSink::finalize).

All zero for a sink that resolves relation endpoints eagerly, which reports everything
through [`per_mapping`](Self::per_mapping) instead. See
[`Resolution`](super::sink::Resolution).

timing.description:
Where the run's wall-clock time went.

`None` from [`extract`](super::extract::extract) itself, which is handed open providers
and cannot know what they cost to obtain. The runner that owns the connections fills this
in, as the `extraction-dbcon` bindings do. Also kept out of `extract` because
`std::time::Instant` panics on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

rows_read.description: Rows the mapping's node produced, before `when` was applied.

entities_emitted.description:
Entities or relations this mapping handed to the sink, which is not the same as
"survived the run" for a sink that defers resolution.

An eager sink refuses a dangling relation at the call site, so it lands in
[`DropReason::UnresolvedEndpoint`] and never here. A deferring sink writes it, counts it
here, and deletes it at [`finalize`](super::sink::ExtractionSink::finalize), reporting it
in [`FinalizeReport::unresolved_endpoints`](super::sink::FinalizeReport) instead. To count
what a run produced, subtract `ExtractionReport::finalize.unresolved_endpoints` from the
total.

deduplicated.description:
Rows that tried to create an entity the sink already had. Not a loss: an object mapping
at event grain names the same object on every row by design. See
[`DuplicateObjectPolicy::Error`](super::blueprint::DuplicateObjectPolicy::Error) for what
turns a repeat into a loss instead.

One increment per row whose entity-creating call found the entity already present, across
mappings, since the sink is what answers.

Resolving a relation endpoint is never counted, so an `E2O`/`O2O` mapping reports zero
however often its rows repeat an id: finding an existing endpoint is the normal successful
case. A blueprint that wants its inline references' repeats counted can name the objects
with their own [`Target::Object`](super::blueprint::Target::Object) mapping.

dropped.description:
Rows dropped, by reason. A row that matches several reasons at once (rare) is counted
once, under the first one detected.

uncoercible_attributes.description:
Attribute values that would not convert to their attribute's declared type, stored as
`Null`. Not a dropped row: the entity was written, with one of its attributes empty.

MappingRef.description: Points a diagnostic back at the mapping it came from.

index.description: Position in the desugared, flattened mapping list this run executed.

label.description: The mapping's own label, if it has one.

path.description:
The JSON path of the authored entry this mapping came from (see `desugar_with_paths`), so
a diagnostic points at what the author wrote rather than a position in the flattened
list.

describes.description:
What this mapping produces, derived from its target: `event "appoint officer"`,
`event -> object relation`, and so on. Present whether or not a `label` was typed.

ExtractionError.description:
Why [`extract`](super::extract::extract) could not run at all, or a non-fatal problem
recorded in [`ExtractionReport::errors`] while it did.

deserializer can manufacture), so this only ever crosses a bindings boundary outbound.

The blueprint failed [`validate`](super::validate::validate), so `extract` refuses to run

A `Source` node names a `source_id` with no entry in the `providers` map `extract` was
given. Fatal.

A predicate's or split's regular expression failed to compile. Fatal. `validate` checks
this, so it should not happen when `extract` is called on a validated blueprint.

A `Join`'s `on` clause named a key column that its input's rows do not carry. Fatal:
dropping the column from the key instead would shorten it, silently turning the join into
a partial cross product.

half-written OCEL that reports success.

Two mappings, or two rows, produced the same rendered id under two different types.
Only reachable under [`IdRendering::Raw`](super::blueprint::IdRendering::Raw). Non-fatal:
the row is dropped (see [`DropReason::IdTypeCollision`]) and the run continues, since
merging the two would fold two distinct entities into one.

The type this row wanted the id for. The type that already holds it is whatever the
sink reports for that id.

Two mappings declared the same attribute of the same entity type under different value
types. Non-fatal: the declaration is widened to a type covering both (see
[`OCELAttributeType::coalesce`](crate::core::event_data::object_centric::OCELAttributeType::coalesce))
and every row converted to it. Reported because the resulting type is then decided by a

conflict is a property of the pair.

Such a sink detects the violation at [`finalize`](super::sink::ExtractionSink::finalize),

A [`SlimLinkedOCEL`] is an object-centric event log where events and objects are referenced
by integer indices ([`EventIndex`] / [`ObjectIndex`]) returned from the `add_*` calls,
and each indexed event/object is an instance of an event/object type (activity / object class)

name: locel_oc_perf_sojourn_per_event
docs: Per-event sojourn time.
For each event with at least one directly-follows predecessor, the sojourn time is
`event_time - latest_predecessor_time` in integer microseconds. Returns one row
`(event_id, sojourn_us)` per qualifying event.
`top_k`: if `Some(k)`, return only the `k` rows with the largest `sojourn_us`, ties broken by
ascending event id, sorted descending. `None` returns every qualifying event.

name: locel_oc_perf_sync_per_event
docs: Per-event synchronization time and the delaying object.
For each event with at least one directly-follows predecessor, the synchronization time is
`max_predecessor_time - min_predecessor_time` in integer microseconds (the span between its
earliest and latest directly-preceding event). The delaying object is the object linking the
latest predecessor (ties broken by ascending object id).
Returns one row `(event_id, sync_us, delaying_object_id)` per qualifying event.
`top_k`: if `Some(k)`, return only the `k` rows with the largest `sync_us`, ties broken by
ascending event id, sorted descending. `None` returns every qualifying event.
